title: What Technical Support Taught Me About QA
excerpt: Technical Support taught me how things actually fail. QA gives me the chance to catch those failures before they ever reach a user.
html:
It's been a while since I've been working across both Technical Support and Software QA, and over time I started noticing something interesting about this combination.

In support, I deal with real user issues, not test cases. I see the impact, investigate, troubleshoot, and stay with it until there's a resolution. In QA, the mindset shifts: now I'm thinking ahead, asking how this could break from a user's perspective.

At some point, I started seeing the connection between the two. Support shows me how things actually fail. QA gives me the chance to catch those failures earlier.

So now when I test, I don't just follow steps. I think about real issues I've already seen. And when I troubleshoot, I don't go straight for a fix. I try to understand what really happened first.

Still learning every day, and beginning to see how much this combination is shaping the way I think and work.
